long_biography.plain_text:
Pop began as a magazine Marquard edited himself while also presenting music on radio and television. It grew through Germany and, after merging with rival Rocky, became one of the German-speaking market's leading youth titles. The German edition of Cosmopolitan supplied a second breakthrough and widened his business from music publishing to premium lifestyle media.

Expansion into Hungary and Poland used launches, acquisitions and international licences to build a cross-border portfolio. Sales of mature magazine operations accompanied a shift into Computec and digital ventures. That willingness to reshape the company eventually left the present group concentrated on gaming, information technology and transactional platforms rather than the print titles that established his reputation.
